common_patterns.redrob: The Redrob docs warn about keyword stuffers; the audit found 1,706 keyword-stuffer shapes and 3,077 nontechnical-title profiles with many AI skills.
common_patterns.global: The resume-screening dataset contains select/reject decisions where reasons often cite missing leadership, system design, or backend experience rather than raw skill volume.
common_patterns.app: Keep Sifter's title/career evidence gate before skill boosts. Candidate skills should only score strongly when the career story supports them.

common_patterns.pattern: Production and ownership language is a stronger signal than buzzwords
common_patterns.redrob: Only 505 Redrob candidates show repeated career IR/search/ranking evidence, while generic production language is common.
common_patterns.global: Global resumes frequently include broad skills, but selected/rejected decisions repeatedly reference applied leadership, full-stack/backend/system design, and practical delivery themes.
common_patterns.app: Boost shipped systems, ownership, evaluation, monitoring, scale, and A/B/testing terms. Keep generic AI terms as weak evidence.

common_patterns.pattern: Sparse public-footprint signals should not be hard filters
common_patterns.redrob: Median GitHub activity is -1, so many candidates have no linked GitHub even when other evidence exists.
common_patterns.global: Global resume datasets often omit external profile links or include inconsistent contact/public-footprint sections.
common_patterns.app: Use GitHub/public activity as a bonus only, never a rejection condition.

common_patterns.pattern: Availability changes hireability but can become bias
common_patterns.redrob: Median recruiter response rate is 0.44, median notice period is 90 days, and only 35.3% are open to work.
common_patterns.global: External resume datasets focus on fit text and often lack availability fields, so behavior is valuable but not universally available.
common_patterns.app: Use response rate, notice, relocation, and activity as capped multipliers and show them separately in explanations.

common_patterns.pattern: Review data must include negatives and traps
common_patterns.redrob: Honeypots and trap-shaped profiles are explicitly part of the challenge.
common_patterns.global: The resume-screening dataset has explicit select/reject labels and decision reasons, proving training data should include both good and bad examples.
common_patterns.app: The candidate review set includes strong fits, maybes, hidden fits, logistics risks, and trap candidates so retraining learns boundaries.
